doc.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Winning Paul Whiteman's radio contest
summary: A playmate's father led her to a children's contest run by Paul Whiteman; she won a trip to Hollywood.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That’s neat. And then when you got to New York, you must have been in some kind of contest for child actresses?

Yeah. I had a little playmate in the building I was staying in and she told me her father had a radio show. So when her father walked in I said I should be on it, and it was a contest for children, and the man was Paul Whiteman.

Yeah. So I won. I had a kilt and a glengarry and all those Scottish things, and I went out to Hollywood. And my mother thought I was going to be, you know, a Shirley Temple. Well they already had a Shirley Temple. So I just settled down and went to school.
